title: Blocked grid routes and path rendering
instructions:
Implement a grid route counter and a deterministic path printer. Coordinates are
zero-based `(row, column)` tuples. Routes start at `(0, 0)` and end at
`(rows-1, cols-1)`, moving only right or down without entering blocked cells.

## Files
- `grid_paths.py`

Implement `path_counts(rows, cols, blocked) -> list[list[int]]`: a table where each
cell contains the number of routes from that cell to the bottom-right destination.
Blocked cells have count zero. Dimensions must be positive integers; any out-of-bounds
blocked coordinate raises `ValueError`. Blocked is an iterable of coordinate tuples;
duplicates are ignored. Types of dimensions and coordinates are guaranteed integers.
Use a dynamic programming approach suitable for a 30 by 30 grid (do not enumerate routes).

`GridPaths(rows, cols, blocked=())` performs the same validation and copies blocked cells.
- `count() -> int`: number of routes; return zero when either endpoint is blocked.
- `path() -> list[tuple[int,int]] | None`: choose a route by preferring right whenever
  the right neighbor can still reach the destination, otherwise down. Include both
  endpoints. Return None if unreachable. For an open 1x1 grid return `[(0, 0)]`.
  Return a fresh list each call.
- `render() -> str`: show this chosen path, or just the grid if unreachable. Rows
  separated by `\n`, no final newline. Blocked cells are `#`, chosen path cells
  are `*`, other cells are `.`. Overlay `S` at the start and `E` at the destination
  only if those cells are unblocked, even if unreachable. On a 1x1 unblocked grid,
  use `S`. Blocked endpoints stay `#`.
